articleMarkdown:
# Studying Jìn (Progress): moving steadily when opportunity arrives

When opportunity and recognition arrive, do the work steadily and avoid letting anxiety over gains and losses pull you off course.

An invitation, a response, or new visibility can bring both anticipation and nerves. Jìn is set amid gifts, audiences, and gradual advancement, yet also describes obstruction, worry, furtive progress, and excessive force. It gives progress different qualities rather than treating it merely as a happy outcome label.

## Identity and line order

Jìn is hexagram 35 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with symbol ䷢. The lower trigram is Kūn ☷ and the upper trigram is Lí ☲; their traditional images are earth and fire, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初六、六二、六三、九四、六五、上九. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line labels designate yang and yin; they are not additional line numbers.

```text
━━━━━━━━━  上九
━━━━ ━━━━  六五
━━━━━━━━━  九四
━━━━ ━━━━  六三
━━━━ ━━━━  六二
━━━━ ━━━━  初六
```

## Hexagram statement

晉：康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Advancement: the lord who brings peace is granted many horses and received three times in a day.

Legge reads the statement as a lord who has helped secure peace receiving many horses and being granted repeated audiences in one day. This is an ancient scene of rewards within ruler-minister relations, not a prediction that the reader will soon receive promotion or a pay rise.

A modern question is how to respond to actual trust when an opportunity arrives. Recognition can encourage us, but cannot replace continued preparation, clear responsibilities, and completion of the work.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Interpretations in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images belong to the commentarial collection known as the Yìzhuàn, usually called the Ten Wings. Below, these commentaries are kept separate from the hexagram and line statements, followed by modern learning applications.

The Commentary on the Judgment explains Jìn as advancing and describes light emerging above the earth. The Commentary on the Images speaks of making one's own virtue bright. The commentaries consider not only being seen by others but making one's conduct clearer.

Today, show ability through reliable actions rather than only improving an image. The quality of progress can be checked through fulfilled promises and clearer understanding, instead of being measured entirely by outside attention.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [hon-sep](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/chinese-change/)

## The six lines, from bottom to top

### 初六 · Leave appropriate room when progress is checked

晉如，摧如，貞吉。罔孚，裕无咎。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Advancing, then checked: steadfastness brings good fortune. Not yet trusted, remain generous and unhurried and there is no blame.

Legge reads the first line as wishing to advance but being restrained, while retaining breadth when trust has not yet been gained. Progress may not be recognized by everyone from the beginning.

If a new idea is not yet accepted, establish what evidence the other person needs and provide an explanation. Do not immediately conclude that you are incapable, or treat every question as an attempt to suppress you.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六二 · Progress and worry can coexist

晉如，愁如，貞吉。受茲介福，于其王母。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Advancing with sorrow: steadfastness brings good fortune. Receive this great blessing from the royal grandmother.

This line advances yet carries sorrow; Legge connects the royal mother with a grandmother's blessing. It preserves an ancient family and political setting.

Feeling nervous after receiving support is not unusual. Clarify what preparation is needed and where to seek help. The royal grandmother image cannot predict that a particular woman will provide resources or good news.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六三 · Trust grows through shared recognition

眾允，悔亡。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: The many give their trust. Regret disappears.

Legge reads the many giving assent as the trust of those around the figure, also connecting it with a shared aim. This does not mean the majority is always right.

In cooperation, let participants see how the task will be completed and take their concerns seriously. Clear communication and actual delivery can establish trust more solidly than constant self-promotion.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九四 · Check whether the way you advance deserves trust

晉如鼫鼠，貞厲。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Advancing like the shíshǔ rodent: even steadfast correctness is dangerous.

Legge gives the animal image of shíshǔ a sense of furtive advancement while retaining uncertainty about precisely which animal it denotes.

If gaining an opportunity depends on concealing information or misleading others, reconsider the approach. This line cannot establish that an actual person is contemptible; nor should all quiet caution be viewed with suspicion.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六五 · Do not let every gain or loss change your direction

悔亡，失得勿恤，往吉无不利。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Regret disappears. Do not be consumed by loss and gain; going forward brings good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.

Legge retains the reading of not repeatedly worrying over gain and loss while continuing an appropriate course. It does not ask people to ignore actual losses or abandon judgment.

Praise at work or not being selected can both provide feedback, but neither needs to overturn your aim every time. Return attention to what can improve, making the facts more specific than your self-evaluation.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 上九 · Excessive advance has costs even when limited

晉其角，維用伐邑，厲吉无咎，貞吝。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Advancing with the horns, used only to attack one's own city: danger, good fortune, no blame; even steadfast correctness brings regret.

The final line uses horns and military attack to describe forceful advancement, while retaining danger and regret. Legge does not call force unproblematic merely because the action is confined to one's own city.

The modern reflection is only a reminder to examine the consequences of forcing progress, not a practical instruction to attack. Continually pressuring collaborators to preserve progress can damage the relationships on which that progress depends.

References: [zhouyi-35](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/晉&oldid=10646579), [legge1882-35](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## A first invitation to share creative work

Original modern scenario

A creator receives an invitation to present her work. Initially delighted, she then worries whether she is good enough. She first learns about the audience and available time, chooses material she genuinely knows, and prepares clear examples instead of trying to appear all-knowing.

When someone questions a point, she treats it as information to check and revises the material. After presenting, she records what was clear and what still needs practice, rather than looking only at the amount of applause.

Jìn here helps her respond to opportunity. Many factors determine whether another invitation follows; the ancient text does not arrange that outcome for her.

## Misreadings to avoid

- Jìn does not predict promotion, rewards, or funding. Ancient horses, three audiences, and the royal grandmother cannot be directly mapped onto present-day resources or dates.

- The means of advancing require independent scrutiny. Recognition cannot justify concealment, coercion, or expansion without limits.

## Three practices

1. Write down a real opportunity that has arrived and the specific responsibility it asks you to take on.

2. Identify one uncertainty that preparation can reduce.

3. Afterward, assess your performance using actual feedback, rather than recording only gains, losses, and self-judgments.

## Related hexagram

### Míng Yí — Darkening of the Light (hexagram-36)

Jìn places light above the earth, while Míng Yí places it within the earth. Reading them together invites reflection on when to become visible and when to preserve things cautiously, without treating visibility as personal worth.

## A closing question

While reading Jìn, ask: am I responding to the opportunity itself, or only chasing the feeling of being seen?

## Textual note

The fifth line adopts the “失” variant explicitly listed in the base edition; the page's main text has “矢”. The fourth line retains “鼫”.
